# Ethotechnics Institute

> Ethotechnics is the engineering discipline concerned with keeping authority, evidence, capability, consequence, and correction coupled tightly enough that increasing machine agency does not silently become unreviewable institutional power.

## Overview
Ethotechnics publishes open standards, mechanisms, diagnostics, and a glossary for organizations that let software make consequential decisions: who gets a loan, a shift, a benefit, or a refund. The object being engineered is the handover of authority, not the model. The practical questions are who authorized this class of decision, on what evidence, until when, who is allowed to object, and what actually changes when they do. The invariant: No system may accumulate consequential agency faster than the institution accumulates the capacity to inspect, challenge, revise, and survive its decisions. The method (https://ethotechnics.org/method) states the seven-stage chain (evidence, authority, decision, consequence, challenge, reconsideration, correction), the six state variables, and the twelve laws that the standards bind.

## Core Frameworks & Standards
- [Standards & Mechanisms](https://ethotechnics.org/standards): Standard clauses, obligations, and patterns mapped to NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act, and ISO standards.
- [Diagnostics & Triage](https://ethotechnics.org/diagnostics): Scoped risk models, burden calculators, and incident triage paths.
- [Finite Stoppability Loop](https://ethotechnics.org/finite): Stoppability and graceful rollback training loop for autonomous systems.
- [Agent Toolkit](https://ethotechnics.org/agent-toolkit): Responsible prompt packs, agent contracts, and teaching flows for AI systems.
- [Evaluation Suites](https://ethotechnics.org/evals): Governance benchmark suites, failure modes, and test cases.
- [Glossary & Taxonomy](https://ethotechnics.org/glossary): Canonical definitions for burden, contestability, repair, and stoppability.
- [Field Notes](https://ethotechnics.org/field-notes): In-depth essays and research dispatches on sociotechnical AI governance.
- [Research Agenda](https://ethotechnics.org/research): Active academic research lines, focus areas, and bridge artifacts.

## Machine-Readable APIs
- [Standards API (JSON)](https://ethotechnics.org/api/standards.json): Full machine-readable catalogue of standard clauses, mechanisms, and validators.
- [Glossary API (JSON)](https://ethotechnics.org/api/glossary.json): Canonical term definitions and semantic cross-references.
- [RAG Corpus (JSONL)](https://ethotechnics.org/api/rag-corpus.jsonl): Full retrieval-augmented generation corpus for AI search and embeddings.
- [Site Index (JSON)](https://ethotechnics.org/api/site-index.json): Complete route and entity index.
- [Crosswalks API (JSON)](https://ethotechnics.org/api/crosswalks.json): Regulatory mapping between Ethotechnics, NIST AI RMF, and EU AI Act.

## Key Concepts
- **Stoppability**: The engineering and organizational capacity to safely halt, pause, or roll back an AI system when harm occurs.
- **Evidence Packs**: Structured, verifiable audit trails and operational artifacts required for GRC workflows.
- **Repair Authority**: Named individuals with organizational power and budget to remediate harm within bounded escalation clocks.
- **Contestability**: Explicit channels allowing affected people to understand, appeal, and reverse automated decisions.

## Commercial Engagements
- [Ethotechnics Studio](https://ethotechnics.com): Commissioned clinical AI safety evaluations, VC diligence, governance architecture, and custom audit design.
